# Comprehension-Debt Review: periodical run 5 (window 2026-10-23 → 2026-11-05)

> **Operator note.** This run is also read as a top-down, independent reading for the Survey research (`docs/plans/survey/notes-2026-11-05.md`, `log.md` and `place-ledger.md`, on branch `claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j`). That tells you what the readings are used for; it does not add scope. **Do not edit that branch, and do not shape findings to fit it.**
> Measure the window from the previous edition in this series to `main` HEAD. Then say plainly whether the window's changes left their areas **better or worse**. Use the per-area verdict table in §3.

**Periodical:** `comprehension-debt` (remit in `lib/periodicals.js`; charter LIN-370). **Mode:** corrective, weekly. At mint, `GET /api/proxy/periodicals` reads it as `due`, 12 days since the last dispatch.
**Repositories:** `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour) is the primary target. `JKershaw/simple-dispatcher` (SD, the runner) is also in scope.
**Type:** review only. Deliverables:

* one committed report, plus its evidence;
* at most \~3 follow-up tickets;
* a summary comment;
* the adversarial second-read comment;
* then Done.

**The window.** It runs from the previous edition's grounding to `main` HEAD.

* **Previous edition's grounding:** LinearViewer `76fc3e91`, SD `1798790` (report `docs/reviews/comprehension-debt-review-2026-10-23.md`, LIN-3825, PR #2069).
* **HEAD at mint:** LinearViewer `af55cb73` and SD `07c88f7`.
* **Size at mint:**
  * LinearViewer: 263 commits; `lib routes public server.js` diff is 367 files, +38.4k / −19.2k.
  * SD: 46 commits.
* **Re-ground everything at your own HEAD**, and state both SHAs. Every specific below is a lead, not a fact.

---

## 0. Audit the scope before executing

Treat everything below as a starting point to **widen**, not a checklist to stay inside. Before walking any module, look for what is in-remit but not listed, and fold it in. Places to look:

* production files born in the window (`git diff --name-status 76fc3e91..HEAD -- lib routes public server.js | grep ^A`; about 80 at mint);
* files deleted in the window, and what still points at them;
* SD files new since `1798790`;
* the seams between sibling reviews (§2d).

If the only change you can make is to shrink this scope, that is suspect. Record what you add in a report section, "What was added to the scope, and why".

Breadth goes into the **search** only. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked, and a near-empty result is a genuine outcome. Follow-ups stay capped at \~3.

## 1. Read prior runs first

* Reports live at `docs/reviews/comprehension-debt-review-<date>.md`. The convention is the `reviews/` entry of `docs/architecture/source-map.md`.
* There are four: `2026-06-12` (LIN-439), `2026-06-25` (LIN-674), `2026-07-01` (LIN-895) and `2026-10-23` **(LIN-3825)**.
* **Read 10-23 in full.** It carries the live ledger, a class list with bounds, and "Notes for the next run" (items 1–7). Build on it. Do not re-derive it.

Ledger status at mint. Verify each item yourself; do not copy these.

* **N1 (stale landing-status claims, top finding) → LIN-3827, Done (**`343d34ec`**, LV PR #2146). The SD half appears not to have landed.**
  * At SD `07c88f7`, three lines still carry the old claims:
    * `opencode-liveness.js:7` still reads "C1 IS INERT: nothing in reapers.js calls readOpenCodeLiveness yet";
    * `reapers.js:1775` still reads "LANDS INERT — nothing calls this yet";
    * `reapers.js:36-38` still cites "opencode arm (:1754)".
  * Find out whether LIN-3827 was scoped to LinearViewer only, or closed without discharging its SD sites. That decides between a reopen-or-comment and a new ticket.
  * Re-run the C1 grep with the wider pattern that 10-23 note 1 asks for ("S1 only", "PR3 will", "for now", "unwired", "until LIN-#### lands").
  * Candidates seen at mint, unverified: `lib/dispatch-entrance.js:884` ("INERT: nothing issues a cascade at end-of-run yet"), `lib/render-ship-biscuit.js:9`, `lib/model-routing.js:53`, SD `config.js:1116`, SD `reapers.js:1233`, and the new SD per-request usage code that LIN-4202 says landed "behind an unwired seam".
  * Context: SD itself ran present-tense rewrites in the window (LIN-4240, LIN-4233). Check whether those swept the same class.
* **N3 (**`[working]` **beat grammar unowned, cross-repo) → LIN-3828, still Backlog.** Both ends moved in the window: SD `heartbeat.js` +20/−2, and `lib/session-telemetry.js` +107/−61. Re-run `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-10-23/comprehension-debt-heartbeat-spike.mjs` and report whether `state:'running'` is still unreachable. Drift 11-05 ruled a sibling contract, `parked-wait-text-cross-repo` (SD writes 4 wait kinds and Harbour reads 1; home LIN-2258). Re-bound class C3 (cross-repo text contracts) at HEAD, and do not re-flag what Drift owns.
* **N4 (rebuild retention rule unenforced) → LIN-3829, Done (**`3861e1ea`**, 2026-10-25).**
  * `scripts/code-shape/retention.mjs` exists. At mint, though, nothing in `package.json` or `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs it; the only `retention` hit is an artifact `retention-days`. Confirm or refute.
  * The **LIN-3742 dashboard rebuild (**`b133a713`**, 10-24) merged a day *before* the check existed.** Run the check over it.
  * Do the same for the rebuilds and moves after it: LIN-3890 Settings untangle (`8bbd6b5f`); the `routes/workspace-api-*.js` moves LIN-3872/3876/3877/3883/3893/3894; LIN-3911's pointer sweep; and the costs rebuild LIN-4195.
* **N13 (**`runStallFailsafe` **unsafe to modify; not promoted last run).**
  * The function now starts at SD `reapers.js:1888` and has grown: Code Quality 11-04 gives a span of 993 lines and rates it HIGH, worsened.
  * Decomposition belongs to **LIN-3544** (Backlog, Code Quality's).
  * This review owns only whether the arm ordering is recoverable. 10-23 asked this run to promote the "ordered list of arms, which orderings are load-bearing" note if it is still absent. First check whether LIN-3544's scope already carries it; if it does, comment there rather than minting.
* **N2 → LIN-3608** (Backlog). **F3 → LIN-692** (Backlog). Re-check them and comment. Do not mint duplicates.
* **N5** (phase graph is documentation-only): `phases.js:104` now says so. Check whether the header at `:7-8` and SD `CLAUDE.md` agree.
* **N6, N7, N8, N9, N11, N12**, the smaller Lows, and next-run notes 4–7 (reader-sourced items never re-derived): close, carry or re-rank each one.

## 2. Run the review

**Altitude.** Work at module/system level: can a cold reader reconstruct *why a module is shaped the way it is* from the code and its nearby docs? This is distinct from the Documentation Review, which works per comment (is *this* comment present, accurate, and why-not-what). Do not re-flag a single missing why-comment that the Documentation Review owns.

**Comprehension debt** is code that works but whose load-bearing rationale cannot be recovered from the code and nearby docs. Flag where:

* **Behaviour is non-obvious and no constraint-comment explains *why*.** A comment that restates *what* the code does is not rationale. It is itself a finding, never a fix.
* **The only explanation lives offsite.** A bare `LIN-###` or PR reference next to non-obvious code is the debt signal. A reference that already paraphrases its constraint in the code is **not** debt. Both repos are dense with ticket tags, so sample whether they paraphrase; do not count them.
* **A newcomer could not safely modify the module.** Apply the cold-hand-off standard: could a cold reader change this module without silently breaking an unstated constraint? If so, there is no debt, and a clean, legible module is a genuine result.

**Weight by risk.** Debt on a critical path, a tricky invariant or an often-changed module outranks a quiet corner.

**Fixes.** The fix a finding implies is a **minimal constraint-note next to the code**, never net-new prose. **Rationale-inflation** (manufactured explanation for self-evident code) is a finding in its own right. Do not flag a module a cold reader can already safely modify.

These classes are **a floor, not a ceiling**. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo. Last run's C1–C6 classes, with their bounds, are a starting list.

### Seed leads: what the window changed

**a. Splits and rebuilds.** Did the reasons move with the code? For each split, read the parent's rationale before the split and check where each load-bearing reason landed. Look for a reason that stayed behind in the parent, was dropped, or was copied into several children.

* `routes/dashboard.js` went from \~3k lines to `routes/dashboard-*.js` (feed, kpis, rulings, summaries, session-state, drilldown, effort). LIN-3742.
* `routes/workspace-api.js` went to `routes/workspace-api-{issue-read,issue-write,scan,audit,feedback,run-evidence,prompts}.js`. Code Quality 11-04 says decisions were "relocated, not removed".
* Settings were rebuilt: `lib/render-settings*.js`, `lib/components/settings-*.js` and `routes/settings*.js` (LIN-3846, LIN-3890).

**b. Subsystems born in the window.** Several are critical-path.

* **Costs and usage** (LIN-4195, all nine pieces Done): `lib/cost-read.js`, `lib/request-usage-{store,fold,intake,loader,vocabulary}.js`, `lib/usage-snapshot-intake.js`, `lib/terminal-marked-task-cost.js`, `lib/row-usage.js`. `lib/task-cost.js` was deleted.
* **Model routing** (LIN-3853): about 10 `lib/model-routing*.js` files and `routes/proxy-model-routing.js`.
* **Home, state and order** (LIN-4016 "the server decides, the browser follows"): `lib/home-view.js`, `home-rows.js`, `home-row-states.js`, `home-pipeline.js`, `task-state.js`, `task-order.js`, `waiting-section.js`, `ruling-settled.js`, `ruling-standing.js`, and `public/home-placement.js`.
* **Run controls and keys:** `lib/run-controls.js`, `key-state*.js`.
* **Deletions:** `lib/next-run.js`, `routes/next-run.js`, `lib/render-next-run.js` and `lib/plan-fee-config.js` were deleted. Look for orphaned references (the F7 class).

**c. Growth inside existing critical modules.**

* `lib/dispatch-store.js` (+1.2k). `addFeedback` is now 448 lines with three decisions. Code Quality rates it HIGH; owner LIN-2398.
* `lib/live-console.js` (+558).
* `lib/task-page-loader.js` (+733).
* `server.js`.
* `public/prompt-section.js`: Code Quality's top finding (a 1,994-line `init` closure); owner LIN-3546. The complexity is Code Quality's. Only its recoverability is this review's.

**d. simple-dispatcher in the window.**

* `hook.js` (+\~830): LIN-4218, one outcome table and one executor for every Stop relay; LIN-4239, status posted last. Check whether the ordering constraint is stated at the table.
* `instance-guard.js` (LIN-796).
* `request-usage.js`, `request-usage-flush.js`, `opencode-request-records.js` (LIN-4199/4202/4203).
* `env-flag.js`, `state-dir.js`, `config.js` (+240).
* The test harness rework: `childEnv`, `stop-group`, the mutation runner, and the baseline (LIN-4220–4224).
* The SD `CLAUDE.md` invariants (LIN-459, LIN-3585, LIN-2446, the phase graph): are they recoverable **at the code sites**?

**e. Seams no single review owns.**

* **The Documentation Review has not run since 2026-10-21.** The whole window is unread at the per-comment altitude. Do not do its job. Do note any module-level debt that sits in that gap.
* **Cross-repo text contracts** (class C3; see N3 and Drift's parked-wait row).
* **Rationale that lives only in** `docs/papers/`**,** `docs/reviews/` **or** `docs/plans/`, not near the code.
* Sibling reports for ownership, to cross-reference rather than re-flag:
  * Code Quality `2026-11-04`;
  * Seams & Tangles `2026-11-05`;
  * Drift & Coherence `2026-11-05`;
  * Stability `2026-11-04`;
  * the cost-tracking review `2026-11-02`.

**Known-issues surfaces to consult:**

* the `## Invariants` section of `LinearViewer/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/architecture/`;
* SD `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/module-map.md`;
* open tickets found through `/search` (constraint-note, rebuild, Theseus, present-tense);
* inline markers (TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX; 0 at the last count in both repos; re-check).

## 3. Write an uncapped report

* **File:** `LinearViewer/docs/reviews/comprehension-debt-review-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`. Run `ls docs/reviews/comprehension-debt-review-*` first, and never overwrite.
* **Evidence:** raw evidence goes in a `docs/reviews/_evidence-<date>-comprehension/` folder. The sibling convention is a date folder with a suffix; check that the name does not collide. It holds the spike re-run, the retention-check output per rebuild, and the widened C1 grep with a verdict per hit.
* **Grounding:** the HEAD SHAs of both repos. Cite every finding as `file:line` at HEAD, never from prior prose. Mark anything not re-derived as reader-sourced.
* **Structure:**
  1. headline;
  2. severity-ranked findings;
  3. **a per-area verdict table for the window** (area | files and tickets that changed it | better / worse / unchanged for a cold reader | the one-line reason), as the operator note asks;
  4. the carried-forward ledger (N1–N13, F3, and the rest from 10-23);
  5. what was added to the scope, and why;
  6. new territory walked, with clean passes recorded as passes;
  7. the class list with bounds;
  8. the trend ledger (add run 5);
  9. notes for the next run.
* **Coverage:** record **every** finding, including the ones not promoted.
* **Landing:** a feature branch (convention: `docs/lin-<id>-comprehension-debt-review`) and a PR against `main`. Merge it yourself once `ci-success` is green; it is docs-only. If merging is genuinely impossible, name the blocker in the closing comment.

## 4. Mint follow-ups: at most \~3, highest severity only

Each follow-up is a well-scoped ticket left in its default state. It carries the problem, why it matters, acceptance and file anchors. Any fix idea goes under an **"Unvalidated idea"** heading.

**Search for an existing ticket naming the same finding first.** Known neighbours: LIN-3827 (Done; reopen or comment rather than duplicate if its SD half is undischarged), LIN-3828, LIN-3829, LIN-3544, LIN-3608, LIN-692, LIN-2258, LIN-2398 and LIN-3546. If one exists, note it in the report and comment on it. Do not mint.

Zero follow-ups is valid. Err toward under-creating.

## 5. Adversarial second-read (required before Done)

After the report and follow-ups exist, a **genuinely separate reader** answers one question cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"*

* **Tier 1** (preferred): a wholly separate session with no memory of this run.
* **Tier 2** (accepted): a fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the report-writing turn. Give it the repos and the window, not your conclusions. Ask it to name its own candidate before it reads the report.
* **Tier 3** (this session re-reading its own report) is **not accepted**.

State which tier you used. Post **one** comment on this task that contains all three of these lines together:

* `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`
* `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's own answer differed from the report's top finding, independent of the verdict)
* `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated`, or `Disposition: no change`

The engine refuses Done until all three lines are present in a single comment. Also copy them into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's answer in full. AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude normally; **DISAGREE is itself the escalation**.

## 6. Conclude

1. Merge the report PR once its required checks are green (see §3).
2. Post a concise, severity-ranked summary comment. Include the merged report path and PR link, the per-area better/worse verdict in one line, and the follow-up identifiers.
3. Move this task to Done. Do not leave it open: an open review task is re-recommended indefinitely.

## **Stay review-only.** Change no code, config, secrets or docs under review, and do not touch the Survey branch. The report and its evidence folder are the only files written. An instruction not to touch files refers to the code under review, never to the report artifact.

## Findings (run 5, concluded 2026-11-05)

Report `docs/reviews/comprehension-debt-review-2026-11-05.md`, PR #2316 (merged `ed46a714`), grounded at LinearViewer `af55cb73` / SD `07c88f7`.

* **Verdict:** the window left its areas more legible. Of 21 areas, 12 are better, 6 unchanged, 1 mixed (Settings) and 2 worse (`task-page-loader.js` and the neighbours of deleted files).
* **Top finding R1:** the stale-status class (C1) recurred, with at least 15 new Harbour sites (one agent-facing). LIN-3827's SD half is undischarged (SD PR #286 conflicts). → **LIN-4301**.
* **Other findings:** R2–R8 are recorded, with comments on LIN-3827, 3828, 3544, 3608, 2398 and 692.
* **Classes:**
  * C1 stale claims: a lower bound of SD 3 + Harbour 15.
  * C1′ deleted-file orphans: 8 + 1.
  * C2 entrance divergences: unchanged.
  * C3 cross-repo text contracts: 6.
  * C4 rebuild commits: 22.
  * C5 line pointers: sampled.
  * C6 F3 sites: 3.
  * Unbounded: the 25 born-in-window files covered lexically only.
* **Adversarial second read (Tier 2):** AGREE / differed YES / fixed in place.

comments.body:
## Adversarial second read (Tier 2)

**Tier:** 2. A fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the report-writing turn. It was given the two repos, the window and the definition of comprehension debt, but none of the report's conclusions, and it saved its own candidate to a scratch file before opening the report.
**Question:** "What is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"
**Reader's own candidate:** the LIN-4195 per-request usage-records cutover. Its decision register (D1–D13, "review note N", "plan N1") lives only in Linear, and stale snapshot claims survived LIN-4203.
**Answer:** one misfile. `lib/session-telemetry.js:400-406` still says, in the present tense, that the runner posts a cumulative `[usage]` snapshot on each Stop. SD `44ab30e` (LIN-4203) stopped that, and the SD twin `opencode-runner.js:585` is stale too. The report had listed the Harbour line as a clean pass; it belongs in R1. It also found one Low exception to "the D-tags are not debt": "the pre-sum fallback (D13)" at `request-usage-loader.js:23`. All 16 of its spot-checks held. It judged R1 real, well bounded and correctly ranked.
**Fixed in place** (PR #2316, commit `9c9f061a`): both lines were added to R1, the §5 clean-pass line was corrected, the D13 exception was recorded, and LIN-4301's scope gained the Harbour line.

Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE
Differed from top finding: YES
Disposition: fixed in place

## Research notes: how run 5 was done

**Grounding:** LinearViewer `af55cb73`, SD `07c88f7`. Both equal `origin/main`; no commit after mint (`git log --since=2026-11-05T19:33:44Z` is empty in both repos), so the ticket's mint-time leads were re-derived at this HEAD, not taken from the prose.
**Full report:** `docs/reviews/comprehension-debt-review-2026-11-05.md` (PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2316). Evidence: `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-05-comprehension/`.

**Process**
1. Read run 4 (10-23) in full and built on its ledger.
2. Ledger re-checks (by the author):
   - The widened C1 grep over both repos: 165 hits, every one with a verdict. The first version used `\b`, which git's ERE on macOS ignores, so it was redone.
   - LIN-3827's SD half: PR #286 is open and now conflicts on `config.js`.
   - The heartbeat spike, rewritten to drive SD's real `buildHeartbeatMessage`.
   - `retention.mjs` run by hand over 22 rebuild and move commits; it is not wired into CI.
   - Orphan references to deleted files.
   - N2, F3, N5, N9, N11, N12, run 4's Lows, and notes 4–7.
3. A new instrument: a forward-reference spike (forward-tense ticket references resolved against the tracker). Of 11 hits, 4 are stale and there are no false positives once date-bound and open-ticket clauses are excluded.
4. Four fresh-context readers walked one area each (router splits and Settings; costs and model routing; Home, keys and the grown modules; SD). The author re-read every promoted claim at HEAD. Lines not re-read are marked *reader* in the report.
5. Sibling reports were read for ownership: Code Quality 11-04, Seams & Tangles 11-05, Drift 11-05, Stability 11-04 and the cost review 11-02. The usage field-name pin (Drift's), the park text (Drift's, home LIN-2258) and the function sizes (Code Quality's) were cross-referenced, not re-flagged.
6. The Tier 2 adversarial second read: AGREE, with one misfile fixed in place (see the comment above).

**Per-layer audit (one line each; sources in the report §1 and §3)**

| Layer | Verdict |
|---|---|
| dashboard split | better (0 refs dropped; the parent header is stale) |
| workspace-api split | better |
| Settings rebuild | mixed (the LIN-1694 cross-repo warning was dropped; dead comments) |
| costs | better |
| model routing | better (stale LIN-3855 clauses; agent-facing `unrouted` example) |
| Home/state/order | better (the header contradicts LIN-4114) |
| run controls and keys | better |
| task-page-loader | worse (assembles Home's run offers silently) |
| dispatch-store | unchanged |
| live-console | better |
| server.js | better |
| prompt-section | unchanged |
| dispatch-entrance | unchanged (N2; `:884` INERT is false) |
| deleted-file neighbours | worse |
| SD hook.js | better (the status-last rule is stated at the table) |
| SD new modules | better |
| SD reapers.js | unchanged (R1a, line-pointer rot) |
| SD test harness | better |
| SD CLAUDE.md invariants at the code | unchanged |
| `[working]` contract | unchanged |
| request-records contract | better |

**Class list:** C1 stale status claims (lower bound: SD 3 + Harbour 15 sites); C1′ deleted-file orphans (8 + 1); C2 entrance divergences (unchanged); C3 cross-repo text contracts (6 members); C4 rebuild commits (22); C5 line-number pointers (sampled); C6 F3 gate sites (3). Unbounded: the module-level rationale of the 25 born-in-window files covered only lexically.

**Surface Assessment: [lands cleanly].** This is a review: the only artifact is a docs-only report plus evidence. The one follow-up (LIN-4301) is comment and doc lines with no behaviour change, and it adds no second representation of anything. The recurrence guard is recorded as an unvalidated idea in LIN-4301, gated on a ruling, because LIN-3827's operator ruling kept the lint out of scope.

## Summary: Comprehension-Debt Review run 5 (closed)

**Report:** `docs/reviews/comprehension-debt-review-2026-11-05.md` and evidence `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-05-comprehension/`. PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2316, squash-merged as `ed46a714`. CI on head `9c9f061a`: CI success, Unit tests, E2E 1–4 and Secret scan all green. Grounding: LinearViewer `af55cb73`, SD `07c88f7`.

**Better or worse, per area:** of 21 areas, **12 better, 6 unchanged, 1 mixed (Settings), 2 worse** (`task-page-loader.js` and the neighbours of deleted files). The splits kept their reasons: 0 refs dropped across the dashboard rebuild and all six workspace-api moves.

**Findings, severity-ranked**
1. **R1 (Medium+, top): stale status claims recurred.** There are at least 15 new Harbour sites in the window: model routing (the LIN-3855 clauses and a dead legacy projection), the **agent-facing** `proxy-instructions.js:678` (`"unrouted": ["run-paragraph"]`), `request-usage-store.js:5-7`, `dispatch-entrance.js:884` (INERT, but live via Home's Stop), `home-view.js:9,15` (contradicts LIN-4114), `session-telemetry.js:400-406`, and 8 pointers to deleted files. LIN-3827's SD half was never discharged: PR #286 is open and conflicts on `config.js`. → **LIN-4301** (new), plus a comment on LIN-3827.
2. **R2 (Medium):** Home's run offers are assembled in the task-page loader, and nothing there says so. Offered to LIN-4301 as optional.
3. **R3 (Medium):** SD line-number pointers rotted (12 of 13 sampled wrong). → comment on LIN-3544.
4. **R4 (Medium):** the Settings rebuild dropped the LIN-1694 cross-repo Claude-family warning (the retention counter can't see this) and left dead comments. → LIN-4301.
5. **R5 (Medium):** `addFeedback` has no phase order at its head. → comment on LIN-2398.
6. **R6 (Medium, carried N3):** the `[working]` grammar is still unowned, and `state:'running'` is unreachable against the real producer. → comment on LIN-3828.
7. **R7 (Medium, carried N2):** the entrance markers are still absent through 10 window commits. → comment on LIN-3608.
8. **R8 (re-ranked Low-Medium, N13):** `runStallFailsafe`'s arm order is recoverable at each load-bearing arm, but the header is stale. → comment on LIN-3544 with the arm list.

Lows L1–L13 are recorded in the report. N11 and N12 are closed; N4 is re-ranked Low (the tool landed but is not in CI); F3 is re-anchored (comment on LIN-692).

**Follow-ups:** 1 minted (**LIN-4301**). The rest are comments on existing tickets: LIN-3827, LIN-3828, LIN-3544, LIN-3608, LIN-2398, LIN-692.
**Adversarial second read:** Tier 2, AGREE / differed YES / fixed in place (see the comment above).
